Made by a Catholic. This module presents the Dhammapada on its own terms. Here is how the Catholic Church speaks of it — you can explore it or leave it.

The Council says that Buddhism, in its various forms, recognizes the radical insufficiency of this changing world, and teaches a way by which people, with a devout and trusting spirit, may reach perfect liberation or supreme illumination.

The Second Vatican Council (Nostra Aetate 2) teaches: “The Catholic Church rejects nothing that is true and holy in these religions.” Their ways of life and teaching often reflect a ray of the Truth that enlightens every person — yet the Church proclaims Christ, “the way, and the truth, and the life” (John 14:6), in whom people find the fullness of religious life.

column4: Hatred or aversion — with greed and delusion one of the three roots of harmful action. It is overcome by mettā, loving-kindness (Dhp 5, 223).
The teaching of the Buddha and the truth it points to — the way things are, and the way to freedom.
The blowing-out of greed, hatred and delusion; the highest happiness and peace (Dhp 204).
The mind is the forerunner of all states (Dhp 1); training it is the heart of the path.
Heedfulness or earnestness — “the path of the deathless” (Dhp 21).
Craving, the root of suffering in the Four Noble Truths.
Right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and concentration.
Dhammapada 5 says hatred ceases by love. Jesus taught: “Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you.”

The Buddha teaches the end of suffering through the end of craving. Christians believe God entered suffering Himself, and that “the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come.”

column7: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with an evil thought, pain follows him, as the wheel follows the foot of the ox that draws the carriage. All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with a pure thought, happiness follows him, like a shadow that never leaves him.
